finding: One site-day in four sits in the weakest margin band
evidence: 251 of 1000 site-days have a margin at or below 0.6 percent; overall margin is 8.91 percent
action: Review the flagged site-days in the action sheet and agree one fix per site this week

finding: WH-South (Atlanta) earns the lowest margin of the warehouses
action: Ask the WH-South (Atlanta) manager for a cost walk-through before the next planning meeting

finding: overtime_ratio is the measure most tied to weak margin days
evidence: Low-margin share is 42.4 percent when it is in the top quarter (250 site-days) against 10.9 percent in the bottom quarter (258 site-days)
action: Set a weekly limit for overtime_ratio and review the site-days above it

finding: Manual sites earn the lowest margin by automation level
evidence: Manual -10.15 percent, Semi-automated 6.03 percent, Automated (AMR/ASRS) 14.93 percent
action: Check whether the Manual gap comes from volume or from labor mix before any investment decision

finding: Overtime Heavy is the most frequent alert
evidence: Raised on 524 site-days; low-margin share 33.8 percent with it against 15.5 percent without
action: Assign an owner to the overtime heavy action and track the count weekly

finding: Unusual site-days carry a different margin profile
evidence: 50 unusual site-days average a margin of -9.33 percent against 7.43 percent for the rest
action: Walk through the unusual site-days listed in the dashboard and log the cause for each

finding: The operational risk segments separate margin outcomes
evidence: Low-margin share is 46.3 percent in the High segment against 1.2 percent in the Low segment
action: Use the High segment as the daily watch list for supervisors

finding: Peak season changes the margin earned
evidence: Peak days 4.99 percent against off-peak 9.62 percent
action: Plan peak staffing against the margin gap rather than volume alone

finding: Moving half of overtime to regular hours has a measurable payoff
evidence: At 50 percent shifted, savings are 608501.43 over 250 days, 1.1436 margin points
action: Test a shift-pattern change at the site with the highest overtime hours

finding: The low-margin risk model beats its baselines
evidence: Logistic Regression held-out AUC 0.998 against 0.5 for a naive guess; rule-based AUC 0.793
action: Use the risk score as a watch list only where the model beats the baselines

finding: Revenue per site-day is not projected better than a naive baseline
evidence: Held-out MAPE 6.88 percent against 1.99 percent for a seasonal-naive baseline
action: Use the projection for staffing plans only if it beats the baseline
